annotations.title: How often haue they exasperated.
annotations.text: Moyses (Deu 9. v. 7.) repeting what had passed in the desert, chargeth the people that they had stil prouoked our lord to wrath, <mn>[1]</mn> from the day, that they came out of Egypt, and always contended against him. And our lord himself expostulating their ingratitude, & often murmuring saith (Num. 14. v. 22.) in the beginning of the second yeare, that they had then tempted him tenne times; <mn>[2]</mn>either by this certaine number signifying an vncertaine, or els chiefly tenne times: for so often we find recorded that they tempted him, and murmured within that smal time more notorionly. First <mn>[3]</mn>nere, vnto the redde sea (Exod. 14. v. 11.) where seing the Egyptians pursuing them, they murmured against Moyses, for bringing them out of Egypt, saying: It had benne much better to haue serued the Egyptians, then to die in the wildernes. Secondly, <mn>[4]</mn>for want of swete water. Exod. 15. v. 24. Thirdly, <mn>[5]</mn>for lack of meate, Exod. 16. v. 3. Fourtly, <mn>[6]</mn>keeping Manna for the next day, contrarie to Gods commandment. ibid. v. 20. Fiftly, <mn>[7]</mn>going on the Sabbath day, also contrarie to Gods commandment, to gether Manna. Ibid. v. 27. Sixtly, <mn>[8]</mn>for want of water in Raphidim. Exod. 17. v. 2. Num. 26. v. 2 Seuently <mn>[9]</mn> in Horeb, adoring a calfe & the image therof. Exod. 32 Eightly, <mn>[10]</mn> repyning for their trauels in the wildernes. Nu. 11. v. 1. Nintly, <mn>[11]</mn> loathing Manna, and burning with desire to eate flesh. Ibid. v. 4. 5 6. Tently, <mn>[12]</mn> desparing to possesse the promised land of Chanaan, after that the discouerers had reported the difficulties, with the force of the people, and of the cities against which they must fight. Nr. 14. v. 1. Al which and the rest, saith S. Paul, happened to them in figure of vs: and are written for our correption (or admonition) that we murmur not as they did. 1. Cor. 10.

notes.text: The people of Israel often murmured in the desert.
The people of Israel often murmured in the desert. Tenne times more notoriously.
